newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY LEAGUE-AUSTRALIA LEAGUE CHIEF QUAYLE RESIGNS.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY LEAGUE-AUSTRALIA LEAGUE CHIEF QUAYLE RESIGNS.

text.p: The Australian Rugby League (ARL)
said on Monday chief executive John Quayle had resigned, ending
his role as a key player in the 18-month battle for control of
the game with media tycoon Rupert Murdoch's rival Super League.
"We tried very hard to talk him out of the decision," ARL
chairman Ken Arthurson said in a statement.
"We have accepted it with the greatest reluctance but John
felt it was in the best interest of the game," he said.
An ARL spokesman said Quayle would make a statement at a
news conference on Tuesday. The date of Quayle's departure was
not released and no replacement has been named.
The ARL last month suffered a stunning reversal in its
18-month battle with Murdoch's Super League when Australia's
Federal Court upheld a Super League appeal against previous
orders banning the rebel competition until the year 2000.
The legal battle enters its final phase this Friday when the
ARL will seek leave to appeal to the High Court, Australia's top
court, against that decision.
Quayle, a former first grade player in Australia, joined the
then New South Wales Rugby League as general manager in 1983.
He oversaw the increase of clubs from 12 to 20 and an
expansion out of its traditional power base in New South Wales
to other Australian states.
Next year will see two rugby league competitions in
Australia for the first time, with the ARL fielding 12 teams and
10 others taking part in the inaugural Super League premiership.
Quayle has been quoted in Australian media as saying he
regards himself as an impediment to any possible peace agreement
between the rival bodies.
